before: [Enter a Master and a Boatswain]
after: [A storm. Thunder and lightning. Enter the Master and the Boatswain.]

before: BOATSWAIN. Can't you hear him? You're getting in the way of our work. Stay in your cabins. You're only making the storm worse.
after: BOATSWAIN. Can't you hear him? You're getting in the way of our work. Stay in your cabins. You're helping the storm do its work!

before: BOATSWAIN. Lower the topmast! Quickly! Lower, lower! Bring her around with the mainsail.
after: BOATSWAIN. Lower the topmast! Quickly! Lower, lower! Heave to under the mainsail.

before: ANTONIO. Hang, you cur! Hang, you insolent noisemaker! We're less afraid of drowning than you are.
after: ANTONIO. Hang, you cur! Hang, you insolent, bellowing bastard! We're less afraid of drowning than you are.

before: GONZALO. I'd bet my life he won't drown, even if this ship were no stronger than a nutshell and leaked like a sieve.
after: GONZALO. I'd bet my life he won't drown, even if this ship were no stronger than a nutshell and leaked like a girl who can’t hold her water.

before: BOATSWAIN. Hold her steady, hold her steady! Set both sails to head back out to sea! Steer her off!
after: BOATSWAIN. Keep her close to the wind! Close! Set both lower sails and steer her back out to sea!

before: GONZALO. Right now I'd trade a thousand miles of sea for one acre of barren ground -- heather, thorns, anything. May heaven's will be done! But I'd much rather die on dry land.
after: GONZALO. Right now I'd trade a thousand furlongs of sea for one acre of barren ground -- heather, thorns, anything. May heaven's will be done! But I'd much rather die on dry land.

before: PROSPERO. You loathsome slave, incapable of absorbing any trace of goodness, capable of every evil! I pitied you, took the trouble to teach you to speak, spent every hour teaching you something, when you, savage that you were, didn't even understand your own thoughts but babbled like a brute animal. I gave your ideas words so they could be expressed. But your vile nature, even though you learned, had something in it that decent people couldn't bear to be around. That's why you were deservedly confined to this rock. You deserved worse than a prison.
after: MIRANDA. You loathsome slave, incapable of absorbing any trace of goodness, capable of every evil! I pitied you, took the trouble to teach you to speak, spent every hour teaching you something, when you, savage that you were, didn't even understand your own thoughts but babbled like a brute animal. I gave your ideas words so they could be expressed. But your vile nature, even though you learned, had something in it that decent people couldn't bear to be around. That's why you were deservedly confined to this rock. You deserved worse than a prison.

before: PROSPERO. ARIEL'S song. Come to these yellow sands, and then join hands. Curtsy when you have, and kiss -- the wild waves hushed. Dance nimbly here and there, and, sweet spirits, carry the refrain. Listen, listen!
after:
ARIEL. Come down to these yellow sands
and take each other’s hands.
Curtsy and kiss, the wild waves hushed,
and dance with nimble steps this way and that.
Sweet spirits, sing the refrain.
Hark, hark!

before: [Burthen [dispersedly, within]
after: [Refrain, from different places offstage: Bow-wow!]

before: PROSPERO. The watchdogs bark!
after: ARIEL. The watchdogs bark!

before: [Burthen Bow-wow]
after: [Refrain: Bow-wow!]

before: PROSPERO. Listen, listen! I hear the proud rooster crowing. Cock-a-doodle-doo!
after:
ARIEL. Listen, listen! The strutting cock
is crowing: Cock-a-doodle-doo!

before: FERDINAND. Full fathom five thy father lies. Of his bones are coral made. Those are pearls that were his eyes. Nothing of him that does fade but does suffer a sea-change into something rich and strange. Sea nymphs hourly ring his funeral bell.
after:
ARIEL. Five full fathoms down your father lies.
His bones have turned to coral,
his eyes to pearls.
Nothing of him fades away
without the sea transforming it
into something rich and strange.
Sea nymphs ring his death knell on the hour.

before: [Burthen Ding-dong]
after: [Refrain: Ding-dong!]

before: FERDINAND. Listen! Now I hear them -- ding-dong bell.
after: ARIEL. Hark! I hear them now: ding-dong, bell.

before: ADRIAN. The climate here must be remarkably mild and pleasant.
after: ADRIAN. The air here must be subtle and delicate in its temperance.

before: ADRIAN. The air here is wonderfully sweet.
after: ADRIAN. The air breathes so sweetly on us here.

before: ALONSO. You're forcing these words into my ears against my will. I wish I had never married my daughter there! Because on the voyage home, my son is lost, and in my estimation, she might as well be too -- she's so far away in Italy that I'll never see her again. Oh, you, my heir to Naples and Milan -- what strange creature of the sea has made a meal of you?
after: ALONSO. You're forcing these words into my ears against my will. I wish I had never married my daughter there! Because on the voyage home, my son is lost, and in my estimation, she might as well be too -- she's so far from Italy that I'll never see her again. Oh, you, my heir to Naples and Milan -- what strange creature of the sea has made a meal of you?

before: ANTONIO. None, man. Everyone idle: nothing but scoundrels.
after: ANTONIO. None, man. Everyone idle: nothing but whores and scoundrels.

before: ANTONIO. She who is Queen of Tunis, who lives ten times farther away than a man could travel in a lifetime. She who could get no news from Naples unless the sun itself were the messenger -- the man in the moon is too slow -- not until newborn babies have grown beards. She from whom -- but who cares about "from whom"? We were all swallowed by the sea, though some of us have been cast ashore again, and by that destiny meant to carry out an act whose past is merely the prologue, and whose future is yours and mine to perform.
after: ANTONIO. She who is Queen of Tunis, who lives ten leagues farther than a man could travel in his lifetime. She who could get no news from Naples unless the sun itself were the messenger -- the man in the moon is too slow -- not until newborn babies have grown beards. She from whom -- but who cares about "from whom"? We were all swallowed by the sea, though some of us have been cast ashore again, and by that destiny meant to carry out an act whose past is merely the prologue, and whose future is yours and mine to perform.

before: STEPHANO. Here, kiss the bottle. Though you can swim like a duck, you're built like a goose.
after: STEPHANO. Here, kiss the book! Though you can swim like a duck, you're built like a goose.

before: CALIBAN. I've seen you there, and I worship you. My mother showed me you, and your dog, and your bush.
after: CALIBAN. I've seen you there, and I worship you. My mistress showed me you, and your dog, and your bush.

before: STEPHANO. Come, swear to that. Kiss the bottle. I'll refill it with new contents soon enough. Swear.
after: STEPHANO. Come, swear to that. Kiss the book. I'll refill it with new contents soon enough. Swear.

before: CALIBAN. Please, let me take you where the crab apples grow. With my long nails, I'll dig up peanuts for you. I'll show you a jay's nest and teach you how to trap the nimble monkey. I'll bring you to clusters of hazelnuts, and sometimes I'll catch young seabirds from the rocks for you. Will you come with me?
after: CALIBAN. Please, let me take you where the crab apples grow. With my long nails, I'll dig up edible tubers for you. I'll show you a jay's nest and teach you how to trap the nimble monkey. I'll bring you to clusters of hazelnuts, and sometimes I'll catch young seabirds from the rocks for you. Will you come with me?

before: CALIBAN. No more dams I'll build for fish, nor fetch in firewood at anyone's order, nor scrape plates, nor wash dishes. Ban, ban, Caliban has a new master -- get yourself a new man! Freedom, hooray! Hooray, freedom! Freedom, hooray, freedom!
after: CALIBAN. No more dams I'll build for fish, nor fetch in firewood at anyone's order, nor scrape plates, nor wash dishes. Ban, ban, Cacaliban has a new master -- get yourself a new man! Freedom, hooray! Hooray, freedom! Freedom, hooray, freedom!

before: FERDINAND. Some painful tasks have a reward that makes the labor worthwhile. Some forms of lowly work are nobly endured and lead to great results. This menial task of mine would be as heavy and hateful to me as anything, except that the woman I serve brings dead things to life and turns my labor into pleasure. Oh, she is ten times gentler than her harsh father, and he is made entirely of harshness. I have to move thousands of these logs and stack them up, under a painful command. My sweet mistress weeps when she sees me work and says no one so noble was ever put to such a low task. But I forget my troubles -- these sweet thoughts of her refresh my labors even when I'm busiest.
after: FERDINAND. Some games hurt, but the pleasure of playing makes up for the effort. Some forms of lowly work are nobly endured and lead to great results. This menial task of mine would be as heavy and hateful to me as anything, except that the woman I serve brings dead things to life and turns my labor into pleasure. Oh, she is ten times gentler than her harsh father, and he is made entirely of harshness. I have to move thousands of these logs and stack them up, under a painful command. My sweet mistress weeps when she sees me work and says no one so noble was ever put to such a low task. But I forget my troubles -- these sweet thoughts of her refresh my labors even when I'm busiest.

before: MIRANDA. Because I feel unworthy -- I don't dare offer what I want to give, and even less dare to take what I'll die without. But this is foolish -- the more my feelings try to hide, the larger they become. Away with shy pretending! Let plain, honest innocence speak for me! I am your wife, if you'll marry me. If not, I'll die your devoted servant. You may refuse me as your equal, but I'll be your servant whether you want me to or not.
after: MIRANDA. Because I feel unworthy -- I don't dare offer what I want to give, and even less dare to take what I'll die without. But this is foolish -- the more my feelings try to hide, the larger they become. Away with shy pretending! Let plain, honest innocence speak for me! I am your wife, if you'll marry me. If not, I'll die unmarried and still yours. You may refuse me as your equal, but I'll be your servant whether you want me to or not.

before: STEPHANO. Of course. I'll kneel and hear it repeated. I will stand, and so will Trinculo.
after: STEPHANO. Of course I will. Kneel down and tell it again. I’ll stand, and so will Trinculo.

before: GONZALO. Truly, sir, you needn't be afraid. When we were young, who would have believed there were mountain people with dewlaps hanging from their throats like bulls, or men whose heads grew from their chests? Yet now we know that every five-to-one investor in exploration can provide good proof of such things.
after: GONZALO. Truly, sir, you needn’t be afraid. When we were boys, who would have believed in mountain people with dewlaps like bulls, pouches of flesh hanging from their throats? Or men with their heads set in their chests? Now any traveler who staked money on his safe return at five to one can vouch for it.

before: PROSPERO. Then, as my gift and something you have worthily earned, take my daughter. But if you break her virginity before all the sacred ceremonies can be performed with full and holy rites, the heavens will let no sweet blessing fall to make this marriage flourish. Instead, barren hatred, sour-eyed contempt, and discord will fill your marriage bed with weeds so loathsome that you'll both despise it. So take care, and let the sacred torches of marriage light your way.
after: PROSPERO. Then, as my gift and something you have worthily earned, take my daughter. But if you take her virginity before all the sacred ceremonies can be performed with full and holy rites, the heavens will let no sweet blessing fall to make this marriage flourish. Instead, barren hatred, sour-eyed contempt, and discord will fill your marriage bed with weeds so loathsome that you'll both despise it. So take care, and let the sacred torches of marriage light your way.

before: FERDINAND. As I hope for peaceful days, fine children, and a long life with the same love I feel now -- the darkest cave, the most tempting opportunity, the strongest urge that our worst nature can produce will never melt my honor into lust, or diminish the joy of our wedding day. I'll think the sun's horses have gone lame or that night itself is chained below the horizon before I let that happen.
after: FERDINAND. As I hope for peaceful days, fine children, and a long life with the same love I feel now -- the darkest cave, the most tempting opportunity, the strongest urge that our worst nature can produce will never melt my honor into lust, or diminish the joy of our wedding day. On that day I'll think the sun's horses must have gone lame, or night itself is chained below the horizon.

before: FERDINAND. I assure you, sir. The pure, cold devotion in my heart cools the fire in my blood.
after: FERDINAND. I promise, sir. The pure, cold snow over my heart cools the fire of desire in me.

before: IRIS. Don't worry about her presence. I met the goddess cutting through the clouds toward Paphos, her son drawn along by doves. They had planned to cast some lustful spell on this man and maid, whose vows require that no consummation take place until the marriage torch is lit. But their plan failed. Mars's hot-tempered mistress has returned again. Her spiteful son Cupid has broken his arrows, swears he'll shoot no more and just play with sparrows, and be nothing but an ordinary boy.
after: IRIS. Don't worry about her presence. I met the goddess cutting through the clouds toward Paphos, her son drawn along by doves. They had planned to cast some lustful spell on this man and maid, whose vows require that no consummation take place until the marriage torch is lit. But their plan failed. Mars's passionate mistress has returned again. Her spiteful son Cupid has broken his arrows, swears he'll shoot no more and just play with sparrows, and be nothing but an ordinary boy.

before: CERES. May the earth's bounty and abundant harvest be yours. May your barns and granaries never be empty. May vines with clustering bunches grow, and plants bow under their heavy fruit. May spring come to you at the latest by the very end of autumn! May scarcity and want keep far from you. Ceres' blessing is upon you.
after: CERES. May the earth's bounty and abundant harvest be yours. May your barns and granaries never be empty. May vines with clustering bunches grow, and plants bow under their heavy fruit. May spring come to you at the latest by the very end of harvest! May scarcity and want keep far from you. Ceres' blessing is upon you.

before: IRIS. You sunburned farmworkers, weary from August's labor -- come here from the fields and be merry! Put on your holiday straw hats and meet these fresh nymphs, every one of you, in a country dance.
after: IRIS. You sunburned farmworkers, weary from August's labor -- come here from the fields and be merry! Take a holiday, put on your rye-straw hats and meet these fresh nymphs, every one of you, in a country dance.

before: MIRANDA. We wish you peace.
after: FERDINAND AND MIRANDA. We hope you find peace.

before: [Exeunt]
after: [Ferdinand and Miranda go into the cell.]

before: CALIBAN. May the plague drown this fool! What are you doing, fawning over such junk? Leave it and do the murder first! If he wakes up, he'll pinch us from head to toe and turn us into something hideous.
after: CALIBAN. May this fool drown in his own dropsy! What are you doing, fawning over such junk? Leave it and do the murder first! If he wakes up, he'll pinch us from head to toe and turn us into something hideous.

before: TRINCULO. Right, right. We steal by the book, if it please your grace.
after: TRINCULO. Right, right. Our stealing runs on a straight line, if it please your grace.

before: STEPHANO. I thank you for that joke. Here's a garment for it. Wit won't go unrewarded while I'm king of this country. 'Steal by the book' -- that's an excellent piece of cleverness. Here's another garment for you.
after: STEPHANO. I thank you for that joke. Here's a garment for it. Wit won't go unrewarded while I'm king of this country. 'Our stealing runs on a straight line' -- that's an excellent piece of cleverness. Here's another garment for you.

before: PROSPERO. Where the bee sucks, there I suck. In a cowslip's bell I lie. There I rest when owls cry. On the bat's back I fly after summer, merrily. Merrily, merrily shall I live now, under the blossom that hangs on the bough.
after:
ARIEL. Where the bee drinks, so do I.
In a cowslip’s bell I lie,
resting there when owls cry.
On a bat’s back off I fly,
merrily following summer.
Merrily, merrily I’ll live now,
under the blossom that hangs on the bough.

before: ALONSO. And Trinculo is staggering drunk. Where did they find this grand liquor that's gilded them like this? How did you end up in this state?
after: ALONSO. And Trinculo is staggering drunk. Where did they find this grand liquor that's gilded them like this? How did you get into this pickle?

before: TRINCULO. I've been in such a pickle since I last saw you that I'm afraid it will never come out of my bones. At least I won't need to worry about flies.
after: TRINCULO. I’ve been so well pickled since I saw you last, I fear the brine will never leave my bones. At least I needn’t worry about flies laying eggs on me.
